diagnostic_evidence.quote: declare the barrier reached when no out-of-basis probe is both significant \emph{and} practically large---operationally, when $\max_\psi e_n(\psi)\le\varepsilon$ for a task-set tolerance $\varepsilon$ fixed independently of $n$

issues.failure_explanation: With the probe standardized (zero sample mean, unit sample variance on the diagnostic set), the numerator of e_n is the squared residual--probe covariance, but the denominator is the uncentered second moment \hat\sigma_r^2 = n^{-1}\sum_i \hat r_i^2, whereas the squared correlation divides by the centered residual variance n^{-1}\sum_i(\hat r_i-\bar r)^2. Hence e_n = (1 - \bar r^2/\hat\sigma_r^2) * Corr(\hat r,\psi)^2, which equals the claimed squared correlation only when the diagnostic residual mean \bar r is exactly zero. On an independent diagnostic set \bar r \neq 0 in general: the fitted intercept forces \bar r = 0 only on the training set, not on the diagnostic set. The stated interpretation is therefore inexact as written.

failure_location.quote: \hat\sigma_r^2 \coloneqq \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \hat r_i^2, \end{equation} is the squared residual--probe correlation, i.e.\ the fraction of residual variance that a linear correction along \(\psi\) would remove

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Center the residuals in the denominator, \hat\sigma_r^2 := n^{-1}\sum_i(\hat r_i-\bar r)^2 (equivalently center the residuals before computing e_n), or add the explicit condition that the identity holds for zero-mean residuals. This is a one-line local fix after which every claim stands unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The interpretation of e_n as the fraction of residual variance removable by a correction along \psi, and hence every \varepsilon-threshold comparison built on it (Procedure proc:residual-diagnostic and both experiments), is slightly misstated. The discrepancy is the factor (1 - \bar r^2/\hat\sigma_r^2), of order 5e-4 relative in the two-branch diagnostic set and about 2e-3 in the Lorenz--96 diagnostic split, so no reported conclusion is numerically affected.
issues.title: Effect size e_n is claimed to be exactly the squared residual--probe correlation but is defined with an uncentered residual second moment
issues.why_classification: The defect is a missing standard local condition in a definition; the forced correction is a single line, no inference or construction needs repair, and because the residual mean is near zero in both experiments the method, thresholds, and all reported numbers survive exactly.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For a probe standardized to zero mean and unit variance on the diagnostic set

taking \(\psi\) to be the orthonormalized Legendre probes \(\sqrt{2k+1}\,P_k\); the factor \(\sqrt{2k+1}\) gives unit variance under \(X\sim\mathrm{Unif}[-1,1]\), so \(e_n\) reads directly as the fraction of residual variance a correction along \(P_k\) would remove
\max_\psi e_n:\quad 0.193\;\longrightarrow\;0.047\;\longrightarrow\;0.0034 ... from \(p=1\) to \(p=3\), crossing \(\varepsilon\) at \(p=3\) and remaining below it for \(p=4,5\)

issues.failure_explanation: The effect size e_n is defined as, and interpreted as, the squared residual--probe correlation (the fraction of residual variance a correction along \psi would remove) only for probes standardized to zero mean and unit variance on the diagnostic set. In the Lorenz--96 experiment the probes are the monomials of the (already standardized) stencil: out-of-basis probes have total degree at least 2, and such monomials are not centered and do not have unit variance (e.g. the square of a standardized component has mean 1 and variance equal to its excess kurtosis plus 2; higher-degree products can have still larger variance). For an unstandardized probe, e_n(\psi) = [Cov(r,\psi) + \bar r\,\bar\psi]^2/\hat\sigma_r^2 rather than Corr(r,\psi)^2 = Cov(r,\psi)^2/(\hat\sigma_{r,c}^2 \hat\sigma_{\psi,c}^2); the two differ by the probe-specific factor \hat\sigma_{\psi,c}^2 (1 + \bar r\bar\psi/Cov(r,\psi))^2 (times the residual-centering factor of ISSUE-001). Consequently the reported values 0.193 -> 0.047 -> 0.0034 are not fractions of residual variance, the maximum over probes is tilted toward high-variance monomials instead of toward the directions that actually remove residual variance, and the stop rule \max_\psi e_n(\psi) \le \varepsilon = 0.01 is evaluated on a quantity different from the one the procedure defines. The selected degree p = 3 is therefore not established to be the selection the stated criterion produces once the probes are standardized.

failure_location.quote: The probe family is the monomials of the standardized stencil up to total degree~6; a probe is \emph{out-of-basis} for a degree-\(p\) fit if its total degree exceeds \(p\). For each fit we compute the effect size \(e_n(\psi)\) of \eqref{eq:effect-size} on the diagnostic snapshots---the fraction of residual variance a correction along \(\psi\) would remove.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Standardize each monomial probe to zero mean and unit variance on the diagnostic set before computing e_n (the normalization the two-branch experiment applies explicitly), then recompute the maximum effect sizes and re-run the stop rule; if the crossing degree changes from p = 3, re-derive the closure and all downstream rollout statistics at the reselected degree. No new theory is required, but the applied selection and its dependent numbers may need recomputation.
issues.overall_effect: The primary diagnostic of the Lorenz--96 closure experiment---the maximum effect size, the p = 3 stop-rule selection, the Regime III (conditional-mean barrier) conclusion for the p = 3 closure, and everything downstream built on \hat f_3 (the closed-loop rollouts, the energy-variance ratios 1.000/0.046, and the learned-scale stochastic closure with ratio 0.531)---rests on effect sizes that are not the defined quantities, with cross-probe comparisons distorted by probe-dependent factors. The two-branch experiment is unaffected because its probes are explicitly normalized.
issues.title: Lorenz--96 diagnostic computes the effect size on unstandardized monomial probes, outside the defining hypotheses of e_n
issues.why_classification: The mechanical fix is local (probe standardization), but it reopens the model-selection step on which the entire Lorenz--96 demonstration, the Regime III conclusion, and the downstream closure and stochastic-closure results depend; whether the selected degree survives standardization cannot be determined from the source, so the complete resolution may require re-running the selection and the dependent experiments---more than a cosmetic edit, though no new proof architecture is needed.
